images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις ἕωθεν πρὸς τὸν πάππον τρέχει· «σήμερον τὴν πομπὴν ὀψόμεθα!»
images.alt_en: Dawn in the house in Kydathenaion: Lysis runs to wake his grandfather Kleinias; Elpis stands by, and Labros looks up hopefully from the courtyard. Spring light.

images.alt_grc: πολλοὶ ἄνθρωποι πάρεισιν ὡς τὴν πομπὴν ὀψόμενοι· οἱ νεανίαι τοὺς ταύρους ἄγουσιν.
images.alt_en: The procession of the City Dionysia passes through the agora: a girl carrying a golden basket, young men leading garlanded bulls, men with loaves and wineskins; the family watches from the side of the road.

images.alt_grc: οἱ νεανίαι τὸ ἄγαλμα τοῦ Διονύσου εἰς τὸ θέατρον φέρουσιν.
images.alt_en: Young men carry the old wooden image of Dionysus into the theatre on the south slope of the Acropolis; priests walk around it. Lysis and Elpis point.
The theatre of Dionysus on the south slope of the Acropolis: a round dancing floor with rows of seats rising up the hill.
A garlanded bull being led to sacrifice (detail from an Attic vase).
A girl carrying a flat three-handled sacrificial basket (kanoun) on her head.
A chorus of men dancing and singing in step around an aulos player (Attic vase painting).

images.alt_grc: ἡ πομπὴ τῶν Διονυσίων· ταῦρος πρὸς τὸν βωμὸν ἄγεται.
images.alt_en: Attic red-figure vase painting of a sacrificial procession: a bull is led to the altar by youths with wreaths, a girl carries the basket (target: a museum photograph, CC0).

images.alt_grc: ὁ Λύσις τὸν Δίωνα ἐν τῷ χορῷ τῶν παίδων ζητεῖ.
images.alt_en: The theatre full of spectators at dawn; below, in the orchestra, a chorus of fifty boys in wreaths waits to begin. Lysis points out his friend Dion, whose face is red.

images.alt_grc: ὁ χορὸς ᾄδει καὶ ὀρχεῖται· ὁ Θεόφιλος ἰσχάδας εἰς τὸ θέατρον ἵησιν.
images.alt_en: The boys' chorus dances in a circle round the aulos player; the choregos Theophilos, in a rich robe, throws dried figs into the rows; Lysis catches one for Elpis.

images.alt_grc: ὁ ἄρχων τῷ Θεοφίλῳ τὸν τρίποδα δίδωσιν.
images.alt_en: The archon hands a tall bronze tripod to Theophilos, who takes it in both hands; the boys of Pandionis cheer, Dion hides his face, Elpis adds a flower to his wreath.
One hand giving a cup to another.
A hand placing a pot on a table.
A running hare and a slow tortoise.
A face, and beside it a theatre mask with open mouth.
A tall bronze tripod cauldron on three legs, the prize of a choral victory.
A piper playing the double pipes (aulos), cheeks puffed, with a mouth-band.

Red-figure vase painting of a victorious choral scene with a tripod, or the choregic monument of Lysicrates (335/4 BC) in the Street of Tripods, Athens (target: museum or Wikimedia photograph, CC BY / CC0).

images.alt_grc: τοῦ ἡλίου ἀνατέλλοντος, πολὺς λαὸς τὸ θέατρον πληροῖ.
images.alt_en: Sunrise over the theatre of Dionysus: the slope packed with spectators on wooden benches; Ariston's family high up at the back, looking down on the orchestra and the stage building.

images.alt_grc: ἡ Μήδεια πρὸ τῆς σκηνῆς ἵσταται· ὁ χορὸς τῶν Κορινθίων γυναικῶν ἀκούει.
images.alt_en: An actor in a pale female mask and long robe (Medea) stands before the stage-building doors; the chorus of Corinthian women listens in the orchestra; Chrysis wipes her eyes, Elpis holds her hand.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Κλεινίας τὸν μῦθον λέγει· ἡ Μήδεια ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος φεύγει.
images.alt_en: Kleinias whispers the story to Lysis; above them, as if in a thought-bubble in vase style, Medea flies off in the chariot of the Sun drawn by serpents.
Two actors in tragic masks and long robes facing each other on a stage.
The wooden stage building behind the orchestra, with a central double door.
A two-wheeled chariot with its driver (Attic vase painting).

images.alt_grc: ἡ Μήδεια ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος τοῦ Ἡλίου.
images.alt_en: Lucanian red-figure calyx-krater, c. 400 BC (Cleveland Museum of Art, attributed to the Policoro Painter): Medea escapes in a serpent-drawn chariot above the bodies of her children (museum photograph, CC0).

images.alt_grc: ὁ κῆρυξ ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ ἵσταται· ὁ δὲ Λύσις ἀνίσταται καὶ βοᾷ.
images.alt_en: Evening in the theatre: a herald stands in the orchestra announcing the verdict; Lysis jumps to his feet in protest while Kleinias pulls at his cloak.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Δημόκριτος καὶ ὁ Ἀρίστων ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ περὶ τοῦ Εὐριπίδου λέγουσιν.
images.alt_en: A dark street under a thin moon: Demokritos and his sons argue with Ariston, hands waving; Chrysis walks quietly with Elpis; a slave ahead carries a small lamp.

images.alt_grc: ὁ Λάβρος ἐκ τοῦ σκότους φαίνεται· ἡ Ἐλπὶς ἀφίσταται.
images.alt_en: In the dark lane a black shape appears; Lysis stops with his arm out, Elpis shrinks back behind her mother, and Labros bounds up wagging his tail.
A man standing upright and still, arms at his sides.
Marble herm portrait of Euripides (Roman copy of a 4th-century BC Greek original), or a vase painting of a victorious poet crowned with ivy (target: museum photograph, CC0 / CC BY).
